stories.headline: Scottish Ambulance Service to take on up to 280 NQPs
stories.body: Backed by £4m of Scottish Government funding, SAS is welcoming up to 280 newly qualified paramedics this year. The Health Secretary met new starters at Livingston on 9 November.
stories.why: A hopeful contrast to the tight NQP job market elsewhere in the UK.

stories.headline: Coroner warns after two women waited 17–24 hours
stories.body: A coroner has sent Prevention of Future Deaths reports to the Welsh Ambulance Service after two women in north Wales fell at home and waited 17 to 24 hours for an ambulance. Hospital handover delays were named as a major factor.
stories.why: Long waits for fallers carry real risk. WAST points to its falls desk and the 45-minute handover target.

stories.headline: Terror response funding falls short of trusts' ask
stories.body: NHS England has set out about £34m to boost ambulance services' terror-response capability, but it appears well short of what trusts asked for. It follows last month's warning that the sector isn't terror-ready.
stories.why: Major-incident readiness depends on kit, training and people on the ground.

stories.headline: JRCALC hypoglycaemia guidance to be reviewed
stories.body: An Essex coroner issued a Prevention of Future Deaths report after a 60-year-old woman treated for severe hypoglycaemia wasn't conveyed and later died. AACE has confirmed the JRCALC hypoglycaemia flowchart is under review.
stories.why: The review includes when patients need hospital. Watch for JRCALC updates.

stories.headline: Dedicated end-of-life ambulance for Bradford and Craven
stories.body: YAS patient transport crews now run a seven-day palliative and end-of-life ambulance between hospital, hospice and home. It builds on a Leeds service that has run for 10 years.
stories.why: Faster discharges at the end of life, and more emergency ambulances free for higher-acuity calls.
